display.purpose: The verdict line at the top of a results sheet. One per screen.

title.purpose: A colourway name or an empty-state heading.

body.purpose: All sentences, capped at a 68ch measure.

label.purpose: Section headings, field labels, table headers, state words.

code.purpose: Run identifiers, option codes, subject numbers — anything cited out loud.

fonts.purpose: One industrial grotesk supplying the label, prose and quantity voices from its width axis.

extensions.shadowPolicy: No shadows exist in this system. Depth is the tonal step from bond ground to sheet white, plus a 1px rule. Heavier 3px rules carry meaning (a finding's head, a recommended stamp, an alert), never elevation.

textures.name: hatch
textures.purpose: Anything unmeasured, unavailable, or in conflict. Survives greyscale, projection and colour blindness, which a grey fill does not.

textures.name: doodle-ground
textures.value: 240px SVG tile of 10 outline shoe motifs rendered at background-size 165px; far layer stroke #e3e7e2 at 1.5, near layer stroke #d0d6d0 at 1.25; scales 0.50-1.15
textures.purpose: The bond stock is printed. Tonal not chromatic, one step off the bond, visible only in the margins because every sheet is opaque. Motifs are collision-packed on a torus so none overlap and the tile repeats seamlessly. Never built from the hatch: hatch means unmeasured.

motion.name: rule-in
motion.purpose: A stage's rule drawn once, only when it completes while the reader is watching. Stages already done at mount are ruled statically via .done without .just-done.

motion.name: rule-travel
motion.purpose: The active stage's rule, a short segment passing back and forth. Reports that a multi-minute run is working. Alternates so the loop has no seam; pauses via [data-page-hidden='true'].

motion.name: rule-breathe
motion.purpose: The reduced-motion stand-in for rule-travel. Non-spatial, so the 'still working' signal survives without movement.

motion.name: scope-in
motion.purpose: Acknowledges scoping the results sheet to one option. Keyed off a scope counter so it never runs on first paint.

motion.name: control-feedback
motion.value: background-color, border-color, color, box-shadow, text-decoration-color 120ms ease
motion.purpose: The only transition on controls. Colour only: nothing on this sheet lifts, grows or slides under the pointer.

extensions.designTarget: 1280–1536px laptop, driven live. No layout breakpoint inside that band.
extensions.theme: Light only. color-scheme is light; there is no dark inversion, because the use scene is a lit desk and an unverified second theme drifts.
extensions.motionPolicy: One material: the rule. Motion is a rule being drawn, traversed, or held, plus 120ms colour feedback. Nothing animates on arrival and nothing changes size or position. Under prefers-reduced-motion, travel and drawing stop while colour feedback and the breathing active rule remain.

narrative.overview:
This is the sheet a footwear developer marks up, not a dashboard. Everything on screen behaves like a working document: cool bond stock, hairline rules, tracked condensed codes in the margins, and quantities set in tabular figures so a column of numbers lines up and can be compared down the page. The reader is an examiner driving the app live while questioning the team, so the sheet is built to be cited out loud — every run, option and customer profile carries a short printed identifier, and every figure sits next to the thing it describes.

Colour on this surface belongs to the data. Besides three marking inks, the only saturated colour anywhere is a generated variant's own measured colourway, sampled from the render by the backend and painted into its chip. That rule is what makes the system honest at a glance: when the pipeline could not read an image, its chip is hatched rather than filled with a plausible guess. The shell takes a deep sample-room slate that owns a real region of the screen, so the page is never a grey screen with one accent colour.

The system is deliberately flat — no shadows anywhere. Depth comes from a one-pixel rule and the tonal step between bond and sheet. Light is canonical and there is no dark inversion: the use scene is a lit desk, read against physical chips. Confirmed anti-references: the AI-product aesthetic and the enterprise BI dashboard. The second matters most, because this system looks superficially like a data product and must never become one: a control room reads one live run; a BI dashboard tiles many metrics for scanning.
keyCharacteristics: Measured and plain — nothing shouts; the figures do the talking.
Precise and instrumented — tabular numerals, exact percentages, dimensionally honest bars.
Warm in language, exact in presentation — plain business sentences, never softened numbers.
Flat, ruled, zero-radius; chips are the only rounded objects.
Chroma is data; the interface itself is near-monochrome.

rules.name: The Measured Colour Rule
rules.body: The only saturated colour on a results screen besides the three marking inks is a variant's own colourway, and it comes from colourway_hex — measured from the render. If that value is null the chip is hatched and labelled "colour not measured." Never infer a swatch from a colour's name.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean confirmed, undecided and critical. They are never used decoratively, never tinted down to soften a result, and no fourth accent is added.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure renders with tabular-nums. Numbers in a column must align digit for digit; a reader comparing options should never re-find the decimal.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A heading carries its own weight. No small label sits above a heading to introduce it — context goes into a ruled field block underneath, where it is a fact with a name rather than decoration.

rules.name: The Hatch Rule
rules.body: Anything unmeasured, unavailable or in conflict renders as a 45-degree hairline hatch, never as a colour. Hatch survives greyscale, a projector and colour blindness, which a grey fill does not.

dos: Do paint a colourway swatch only from colourway_hex; hatch it when that value is null.
Do set every figure in tabular numerals, and put the number next to the thing it measures.
Do size every bar and segment to its real value, with the written count beside it.
Do print a citable identifier — run, option, subject — wherever a figure can be asked about.
Do keep colour on the data: slate for the shell, three inks for meaning, variant colour for variants.
Do state what the system does not know, in the place the reader would otherwise assume it does.
Do give every control its hover, focus-visible, disabled, loading, error and empty state.
donts: Don't add a shadow. Depth is the tonal step and the hairline.
Don't put a small label above a heading. The heading speaks for itself.
Don't introduce a fourth accent colour, or tint a marking ink to soften a result.
Don't render a figure that did not come from an API response — including in empty and loading states.
Don't nest a bordered box inside a bordered box.
Don't reach for a chart library. The written numbers and the ruled bar are the chart.
Don't use a Unicode glyph as an icon. Marks are drawn SVG at 1.5 stroke in a 16px box.
Don't imply the system covers categories beyond footwear.
